summary: Gary Urton works in history, archaeology, and related fields. He studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He held posts at Colgate University and Harvard University, alongside a visiting post at EHESS.

Gaspare Gorresio was an Indologist who studied at the Diocesan Seminary of Mondovi and the University of Turin under Amedeo Peyron, later studying under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He held posts at Turin's Military Academy, University, and Royal Library.

Gaston Paris was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the École des chartes and under Friedrich Christian Diez. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1872) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Polytechnique from circa 1898 to 1900.
Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Gauri Viswanathan is a scholar of Indology who studied at the University of Delhi and Columbia University. She taught English at the University of Delhi and was appointed Class of 1933 Professor and South Asia Institute director at Columbia.

Gavin D'Costa works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge and the University of Birmingham under John Hick. His career includes posts at the West London Institute of Higher Education and the University of Bristol.

Gavin Flood is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held positions at the University of Wales Lampeter, University of Stirling, University of Oxford, and Yale-NUS College.

Geshe Gedün Lodrö was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and under Khensur Ngawang Lekden, later holding posts at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Virginia.
Geetha K. Wilson is an Indology scholar. Attested in 2026, she studied at the University of Tübingen as a doctoral student under Claire Maes and served on the Tübingen faculty.

Gelek is a scholar of Tibetology. He held a researcher post at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998) and served as a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford and visiting lecturer at UC Berkeley.

Gelek Rimpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Monastery, the Young Lamas Home School, and Cornell University, and under teachers including Ling Rinpoche and Trijang Rinpoche. He directed Tibet House New Delhi.

Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tango Monastery, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, receiving training from traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (~1965–1974) and as a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2006.

Genchi Kato was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue. He held professorships with the Imperial Japanese Army, the University of Tokyo, Kokugakuin University, and Taisho University.
Gendun Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He founded Dhagpo Kagyu Ling and served as its abbot and retreat master from circa 1977 to 1997.

Gendün Chöphel worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Drisha, Labrang, Kumbum, and Drepung Monasteries, under teachers including Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso. In 1941, he was associated with the Maha Bodhi Society.

Genjun Sasaki was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Kyoto University, studying under figures including Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at the University of Hamburg, Harvard University, Otani University, and Osaka University.
Genro was a Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and held the post of head monk (第一座) at Myōshin-ji.
Genryu Kagamishima was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and later served as a professor there from circa 1959 to 1983.
